hr-process-automation.overview: An RPA workflow that builds the manpower report. It tracks employees role-wise and branch-wise, applies the business rules and status filters the report needs, and sends each region its own summary by email.
hr-process-automation.businessProblem: The business needed role-wise, branch-wise and region-wise visibility of manpower, which meant pulling the data, mapping it, applying the reporting rules and summarising it by region every cycle.
workflow: Apply lookup and mapping logic where the report needs it
Filter on employee status where required

multi-product-mis.overview: Several MIS reports, each automated against the sources it actually uses. Across the estate those sources include SFTP, FTP, Amazon S3, databases, email, Excel and CSV — no single report uses all of them. The steps below are the typical shape; each report runs the subset it needs.
workflow: Pull the source data — file server, bucket, database or mailbox, depending on the report
Extract it with the RPA bot
Process it with SQL and Python

challenges.challenge: Many reports, many data sources, each with its own requirements.
challenges.resolution: RPA combined with SQL, Python and Excel processing, and a standardised way of generating the reports.

challenges.challenge: Excel processing too complex for basic RPA activities.
challenges.resolution: Python, VBA, Pivot Tables, VLOOKUP and business logic, used together rather than forcing everything through the bot.

decisions.decision: Use Python alongside RPA where data processing or Excel work becomes complex.
decisions.why: Python gives flexibility for data transformation, calculation and Excel processing.

decisions.decision: Use SQL for extraction and filtering on the database side.
decisions.why: It avoids moving data unnecessarily and prepares the business data before downstream processing.

decisions.decision: Use Excel, VBA, Pivot Tables and VLOOKUP where the output has to be Excel.
decisions.why: Many business stakeholders consume and work with their reports in Excel.

decisions.decision: Integrate with whichever source each process actually uses — SFTP, FTP, S3, database or email.
decisions.why: The automation should work with the real enterprise source rather than force every workflow into one integration pattern.

lessonsLearned: Understand the business process before automating it.
RPA is stronger combined with SQL, Python and Excel than when the RPA tool is treated as the only technology.
Complex reporting needs business-rule understanding as much as technical processing.
Automation should handle exceptions rather than assume every input is perfect.

new-los-reporting.overview: Reporting for a new loan origination system, set out as a report master and a field-level specification covering the loan lifecycle for LAP and Home Loan — lead and sourcing, application, documents, credit, legal and technical, sanction, documentation, disbursement, TAT and ageing, rejections, audit, API monitoring, management reporting, insurance and Account Aggregator.
scale: Two products — LAP and Home Loan

automationedge-migration.overview: An evaluation of AutomationEdge as an enterprise RPA platform alongside the existing TruBot estate, followed by a planned migration. The figures below are the planned scope of the programme — not processing volumes and not measured impact. The migration is in progress.

challenges.challenge: A large migration programme with many processes to move.
challenges.resolution: Parallel development tracks, reusable components and batch-wise testing.

challenges.challenge: Different vendor expectations during the POC.
challenges.resolution: Aligning scope, evaluation criteria and acceptance requirements before proceeding.

lessonsLearned: Reusable components matter more as the number of automations grows.
Testing should happen continuously, not only at the end of a large programme.
